descVi: Diễn đạt sắc bén, chính xác và tự nhiên như bản xứ — IELTS 7.5–8.0.

words.definitionEn: To publicly support a policy, idea, or course of action.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our neighbours advocate planting more trees along the street.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many health professionals advocate regular physical activity as an affordable way to prevent chronic disease.

words.definitionEn: To assign resources to particular people, activities, or purposes.
words.exampleDailyEn: We allocated one cupboard to all our baking equipment.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities should allocate more funding to public transport in areas with limited access to essential services.

words.definitionEn: To reach a goal or level, usually through effort.
words.exampleDailyEn: After months of practice, she attained her target swimming speed.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Students from disadvantaged backgrounds may need additional support to attain the qualifications required for university entry.

words.definitionEn: to stop happening or doing something
words.exampleDailyEn: The bells finally ceased ringing just before midnight.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Factories should cease discharging untreated wastewater into rivers to protect aquatic ecosystems and safeguard public health.

words.definitionEn: The quality of being clear and easy to understand.
words.exampleDailyEn: I appreciate the clarity of your instructions for this game.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Greater clarity in public health advice can help people make informed decisions about their daily habits.

words.definitionEn: Collect information from different sources and arrange it together.
words.exampleDailyEn: We compiled a playlist for our long train journey.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers compiled data from several hospitals to examine the relationship between air pollution and childhood asthma.

words.definitionEn: Something that limits what you can do.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our main constraint is the size of the kitchen.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Financial constraints prevent many local authorities from investing adequately in reliable public transport.

words.definitionEn: to present information in a misleading or inaccurate way
words.exampleDailyEn: That edited clip distorts what I actually said.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Selective reporting can distort public understanding of environmental issues and weaken support for necessary reforms.

words.definitionEn: To slow down or prevent a process or activity.
words.exampleDailyEn: Cold weather can inhibit the growth of these plants.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Fear of making mistakes can inhibit students from participating actively in classroom discussions and collaborative tasks.

words.definitionEn: become stronger or more extreme, or make something so
words.exampleDailyEn: The rain intensified as we hurried towards the station.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Rising temperatures may intensify water shortages in regions that already experience long periods of drought.

words.definitionEn: something that happens, especially something noticeable
words.exampleDailyEn: Power cuts are a rare occurrence in our village.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Improved drainage systems can reduce the occurrence of flooding in densely populated urban areas.

words.definitionEn: next to or very near something
words.exampleDailyEn: We booked adjacent rooms so the children could stay nearby.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Residents in areas adjacent to the airport often experience high levels of noise pollution.

words.definitionEn: Unwillingness or hesitation to do something.
words.exampleDailyEn: With obvious reluctance, Leo handed his favourite toy back.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Some commuters show reluctance to use public transport because services are infrequent and unreliable.

words.definitionEn: the movement of people or goods between places
words.exampleDailyEn: The glasses broke while they were in transit.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Investment in public transit can reduce traffic congestion and improve access to employment in growing cities.

words.definitionEn: Music played to support a singer or main instrument.
words.exampleDailyEn: My sister sang while I played the piano accompaniment.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Learning to provide musical accompaniment can help students develop listening skills and cooperate more effectively with others.

words.definitionEn: Moving between regions regularly, often with the seasons.
words.exampleDailyEn: Migratory birds gather by the lake every spring.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Protecting wetlands along migratory routes is essential because many bird species depend on these habitats for food and rest.

words.definitionEn: A lack of enough of something necessary.
words.exampleDailyEn: A blood test revealed that I had an iron deficiency.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Nutritional deficiency among children can affect physical growth and reduce their ability to concentrate at school.

words.definitionEn: a poor farmer working a small plot of land
words.exampleDailyEn: The painting shows a peasant carrying vegetables home.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Historically, peasant families often depended on a single harvest, making them particularly vulnerable to drought.

words.definitionEn: An achievement requiring great skill, strength, or courage.
words.exampleDailyEn: Carrying that huge sofa upstairs was quite a feat.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Building a railway across mountainous terrain remains an impressive feat of engineering, even with modern technology.

words.definitionEn: A promise intended to remove doubt or worry.
words.exampleDailyEn: She gave me her assurance that dinner was ready.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Residents sought an assurance from the council that the new development would not reduce access to public parks.

words.definitionEn: To change a document, rule, or plan to improve it.
words.exampleDailyEn: Please amend the booking to include one extra guest.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Parliament may amend existing legislation to ensure that remote workers receive the same protections as office employees.

words.definitionEn: to have particular people or things as parts
words.exampleDailyEn: The gift set comprises soap, lotion, and a towel.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The proposed transport network will comprise bus routes and cycle lanes connecting residential areas with employment centres.

words.definitionEn: to begin something or start happening
words.exampleDailyEn: The evening concert will commence after a short welcome.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Construction of the new railway will commence once the environmental assessment has been completed.

words.definitionEn: to form an idea or imagine something
words.exampleDailyEn: She conceived the idea while walking through the park.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Urban planners must conceive new ways of accommodating population growth without sacrificing green spaces or affordable housing.

words.definitionEn: To reproduce conditions or processes for testing, training, or study.
words.exampleDailyEn: This driving game simulates icy roads surprisingly well.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers simulate extreme weather conditions to assess how new building materials perform under environmental stress.

words.definitionEn: very small in amount, effect, or importance
words.exampleDailyEn: The new tyres made only a marginal difference.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Despite substantial investment, the programme produced only marginal improvements in public transport reliability across the city.

words.definitionEn: A publication released regularly, containing articles on particular subjects.
words.exampleDailyEn: The library keeps that periodical beside the newspapers.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Academic periodicals allow researchers to share findings, although subscription costs can limit access for smaller institutions.

words.definitionEn: proving something clearly and leaving no reasonable doubt
words.exampleDailyEn: The camera footage provided conclusive proof of what happened.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers need conclusive evidence before recommending major changes to national policies on childhood nutrition.

words.definitionEn: Having a limit in size, amount, or duration
words.exampleDailyEn: Our holiday budget is finite, so choose carefully.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments must recognise that natural resources are finite and encourage industries to reduce unnecessary consumption.

words.definitionEn: by an amount that is large enough to notice
words.exampleDailyEn: The room felt appreciably warmer after we closed the window.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Expanding reliable public transport could appreciably reduce traffic congestion and improve air quality in urban areas.

words.definitionEn: Someone who lives in or uses a room, building, or vehicle.
words.exampleDailyEn: The previous occupant left some curtains in the flat.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Building regulations should ensure that every occupant can leave safely in the event of a fire.

words.definitionEn: A lack of interest, concern, or emotional response.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her indifference surprised me when I shared my exciting news.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public indifference to local elections can weaken accountability and reduce the quality of democratic representation.

words.definitionEn: difficult or impossible to reach or enter
words.exampleDailyEn: Heavy snow made the mountain cabin inaccessible all weekend.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public services remain inaccessible to many rural residents because reliable transport and internet connections are lacking.

words.definitionEn: to adapt a story or event for performance
words.exampleDailyEn: Our class will dramatize a short story next week.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Television producers often dramatize historical events to attract viewers, but this can blur the distinction between fact and fiction.

words.definitionEn: The children or young of a person, animal, or plant.
words.exampleDailyEn: The mother duck led her offspring safely across the path.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many species invest considerable energy in protecting their offspring, which increases the young animals' chances of survival.

words.definitionEn: Very serious or intense.
words.exampleDailyEn: The village faced an acute water shortage last summer.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An acute shortage of affordable housing forces many young workers to live far from their workplaces.

words.definitionEn: relating to a territory controlled by a foreign country
words.exampleDailyEn: Our guide showed us several buildings from the colonial period.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Colonial rule often reshaped local economies by directing agricultural production towards the needs of distant markets.

words.definitionEn: The ability to continue despite tiredness, pain, or difficulty.
words.exampleDailyEn: Swimming every morning has really improved my endurance.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular physical activity builds endurance and helps people manage the demands of an increasingly sedentary lifestyle.

words.definitionEn: To keep something within particular limits
words.exampleDailyEn: Please confine your muddy boots to the porch.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers should not confine their investigation to wealthy neighbourhoods when studying access to public transport.

words.definitionEn: A change made to a law, document, or proposal.
words.exampleDailyEn: We agreed on one small amendment to the contract.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The proposed amendment would require employers to provide safer working conditions for temporary staff.

words.definitionEn: an introduction that helps people adjust to a new setting
words.exampleDailyEn: During orientation, a student guide showed us the library.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A comprehensive orientation programme can help international students understand academic expectations and access essential support services.

words.definitionEn: Discuss something with others before making a decision.
words.exampleDailyEn: The coaches conferred quietly before choosing the final team.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Universities often confer honorary degrees on individuals who have made outstanding contributions to science or public service.

words.definitionEn: an idea or understanding of what something is like
words.exampleDailyEn: His conception of a perfect holiday involves no phones.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Access to green spaces can broaden children's conception of nature beyond what they learn in classrooms.

words.definitionEn: Improve something by making small, careful changes
words.exampleDailyEn: I refined my recipe by adding less sugar.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools can refine their teaching methods by collecting regular feedback from students with different learning needs.

words.definitionEn: Pay part of the cost of an activity or service
words.exampleDailyEn: My employer subsidizes lunch at the office cafeteria.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments could subsidize public transport to make commuting more affordable and reduce urban traffic.

words.definitionEn: A surprising fact that becomes known.
words.exampleDailyEn: His revelation about the hidden garden surprised us all.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Recent revelations about industrial pollution have increased public pressure for stricter environmental regulations and greater corporate transparency.

words.definitionEn: To represent or indicate something.
words.exampleDailyEn: On this map, blue lines denote rivers and streams.
words.exampleIeltsEn: In scientific diagrams, different colours often denote distinct materials, allowing readers to interpret complex structures more easily.

words.definitionEn: to balance or reduce the effect of something
words.exampleDailyEn: My shorter commute offsets the higher rent here.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Planting trees can offset some carbon emissions, but reducing fossil fuel consumption remains essential.

words.definitionEn: Planned or expected to happen or appear soon.
words.exampleDailyEn: We bought new walking boots for our forthcoming trip.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The forthcoming report will assess whether investment in public transport has reduced urban air pollution.

words.definitionEn: A wall or screen that divides a space into sections.
words.exampleDailyEn: A wooden partition separates our kitchen from the dining area.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Movable partitions allow schools to adapt classroom spaces for group discussions, independent study, and larger community events.

words.definitionEn: A strong feeling that someone or something deserves no respect
words.exampleDailyEn: He showed contempt for my suggestion by laughing.
words.exampleIeltsEn: When officials treat public concerns with contempt, trust in democratic institutions can decline significantly.

words.definitionEn: Find your position or become familiar with your surroundings.
words.exampleDailyEn: I used the river to orientate myself in town.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Universities should orientate their support services towards the needs of students adjusting to life away from home.

words.definitionEn: to show or describe something in art, images, or words
words.exampleDailyEn: This painting depicts children playing beside a quiet lake.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Films often depict urban life as exciting, overlooking the isolation that many residents experience in large cities.

words.definitionEn: an organism such as a mushroom, mould, or yeast
words.exampleDailyEn: A strange orange fungus was growing on the fallen tree.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Some types of fungus help maintain healthy forests by breaking down dead wood and recycling nutrients.

words.definitionEn: Continuing for a long time, especially a medical condition
words.exampleDailyEn: Gentle swimming helps her manage her chronic back pain.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Chronic staff shortages can reduce the quality of healthcare and increase pressure on existing medical workers.

words.definitionEn: To honour a person or event by remembering them publicly
words.exampleDailyEn: We planted a tree to commemorate our grandfather's life.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public ceremonies commemorate historical events and help younger generations understand the experiences that shaped their communities.

words.definitionEn: A strap used by a rider to guide a horse.
words.exampleDailyEn: The rider gently pulled the reins to stop the horse.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments may need to rein in excessive spending while protecting essential services such as education and healthcare.

words.definitionEn: To be the parts that form a whole
words.exampleDailyEn: Vegetables constitute most of the food in our fridge.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Rising housing costs constitute a major barrier to financial independence for young adults in large cities.

words.definitionEn: To act against a law, rule, or agreement.
words.exampleDailyEn: Leaving your car here violates the building's parking rules.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Collecting personal data without informed consent may violate citizens' privacy and undermine public trust in digital services.

words.definitionEn: Trusted as accurate because of expert knowledge.
words.exampleDailyEn: This gardening guide offers authoritative advice on growing vegetables.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Students should consult authoritative sources when evaluating health claims shared widely through social media platforms.

words.definitionEn: make an action or process easier
words.exampleDailyEn: These sliding doors facilitate access for people using wheelchairs.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Digital platforms can facilitate collaboration between students in different countries, allowing them to exchange ideas more easily.

words.definitionEn: A standard used to judge something or make a decision.
words.exampleDailyEn: Price was my main criterion when choosing a bicycle.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Environmental impact should be a key criterion when governments assess proposals for new transport infrastructure.

words.definitionEn: A small change that makes something better or more effective.
words.exampleDailyEn: One small refinement made the chair much more comfortable.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Continued refinement of water treatment methods can improve public health while reducing the cost of supplying clean water.

words.definitionEn: Money provided to support activities or keep prices lower.
words.exampleDailyEn: A government subsidy helped us install solar panels at home.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Targeted subsidies for public transport can make commuting more affordable while encouraging people to use their cars less.

words.definitionEn: A misleading change in how facts or ideas are presented.
words.exampleDailyEn: His version of our conversation was a complete distortion.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The distortion of scientific findings in news reports can undermine public understanding of health risks.

words.definitionEn: a departure from an expected route, rule, or behaviour
words.exampleDailyEn: A small deviation from our route revealed a quiet beach.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Any significant deviation from established safety procedures should be investigated to prevent accidents in the workplace.

words.definitionEn: The gradual gathering of something, or the amount gathered.
words.exampleDailyEn: An accumulation of dust covered the old wooden shelves.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The accumulation of plastic waste in oceans threatens marine wildlife and creates lasting challenges for coastal communities.

words.definitionEn: Always, or on every occasion.
words.exampleDailyEn: My brother invariably falls asleep during long train journeys.
words.exampleIeltsEn: In this study, participants with longer commuting times invariably reported having less time for leisure activities.

words.definitionEn: to be directly next to or share a boundary with something
words.exampleDailyEn: Our garden adjoins a quiet park with tall oak trees.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Residential areas that adjoin industrial sites may require additional measures to protect residents from noise and pollution.

words.definitionEn: to bring a feeling, memory or image into someone's mind
words.exampleDailyEn: The smell of fresh bread evokes memories of home.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Traditional music can evoke a strong sense of belonging among people living far from their homeland.

words.definitionEn: to move upwards or rise to a higher position
words.exampleDailyEn: We watched the balloon ascend slowly into the clear sky.
words.exampleIeltsEn: As hikers ascend the mountain, they encounter distinct vegetation zones shaped by changing temperatures and moisture levels.

words.definitionEn: Containing many carefully arranged details or parts.
words.exampleDailyEn: The cake had elaborate flowers made entirely from icing.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments sometimes develop elaborate plans for educational reform without consulting the teachers who will implement them.

words.definitionEn: a hunting bird with sharp claws and a curved beak
words.exampleDailyEn: A hawk circled slowly above the open field.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Protecting woodland habitats helps maintain hawk populations, which play an important role in controlling small mammals.

words.definitionEn: extreme tiredness caused by effort, stress, or illness
words.exampleDailyEn: After the long hike, fatigue made my legs shake.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Persistent fatigue can reduce employees' concentration and increase the likelihood of accidents in the workplace.

words.definitionEn: Connected with a god or coming from a god
words.exampleDailyEn: The painting shows divine light surrounding a heavenly figure.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many ancient societies believed that rulers received divine authority, which helped strengthen their political power.

words.definitionEn: Fair and respectful behaviour towards opponents in sport
words.exampleDailyEn: Helping her opponent up showed real sportsmanship.
words.exampleIeltsEn: School competitions should reward sportsmanship as well as achievement to encourage respect and cooperation among students.

words.definitionEn: to become smaller or weaker, or make something so
words.exampleDailyEn: The pain in my ankle gradually diminished overnight.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Investment in reliable public transport can diminish dependence on private cars and improve air quality in crowded cities.

words.definitionEn: to make something no longer legally or officially acceptable
words.exampleDailyEn: Opening the device yourself may invalidate its warranty.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A sample that excludes older adults may invalidate conclusions about the health needs of the wider population.

words.definitionEn: The beginning of something, especially an official activity
words.exampleDailyEn: We heard a whistle at the commencement of play.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Environmental assessments should be completed before the commencement of construction to minimise potential damage to local ecosystems.

words.definitionEn: To cause a process or activity to begin.
words.exampleDailyEn: Someone needs to initiate a conversation about the noise.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities should initiate programmes that encourage residents to recycle household waste more effectively.

words.definitionEn: a particular area of knowledge, activity, or responsibility
words.exampleDailyEn: Electrical repairs are my brother's domain, not mine.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Environmental protection should not be regarded as the exclusive domain of scientists, since public participation is essential.

words.definitionEn: To calculate an amount or result, often using a computer.
words.exampleDailyEn: This app computes the cost of our weekly shopping.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers compute average temperatures from satellite data to assess long-term changes in the global climate.

words.definitionEn: the usefulness of something for a particular purpose
words.exampleDailyEn: This folding table offers real utility in our tiny kitchen.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Reliable access to basic utilities is essential for improving public health and supporting economic development in rural communities.

words.definitionEn: Impressive language that may lack sincerity or practical substance.
words.exampleDailyEn: We need real help, not more rhetoric about teamwork.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments must move beyond environmental rhetoric and introduce measurable policies to reduce industrial pollution.

words.definitionEn: Separate and distinct rather than joined or continuous.
words.exampleDailyEn: We divided the project into three discrete tasks.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers classified participants into discrete groups to compare the effects of different teaching methods.

words.definitionEn: the complete removal of something unwanted or unnecessary
words.exampleDailyEn: Regular cleaning helps with the elimination of unpleasant kitchen smells.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The elimination of unnecessary packaging could significantly reduce household waste and lower the environmental impact of shopping.

words.definitionEn: continuing for a long time or happening repeatedly
words.exampleDailyEn: A persistent cough kept me awake throughout the night.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Persistent shortages of affordable housing can force young adults to delay leaving their family homes.

words.meaningVi: Một hỗn hợp ồn ào, khó chịu của những tiếng ồn liên tục
words.definitionEn: A loud, unpleasant mixture of continuing noises.
words.exampleDailyEn: We could barely hear each other above the din.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The constant din of traffic can reduce residents' quality of life and disturb their sleep.

words.definitionEn: to become stronger or make a feeling or effect stronger
words.exampleDailyEn: The sudden silence only heightened my curiosity about the surprise.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Repeated droughts may heighten public concern about water shortages and encourage governments to invest in conservation.

words.definitionEn: a market with many small shops or stalls
words.exampleDailyEn: We bought fragrant spices at the crowded bazaar.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Traditional bazaars can attract tourists while providing local craftspeople with opportunities to sell their products directly.

words.definitionEn: Relating to beauty or the appreciation of beautiful things.
words.exampleDailyEn: The wooden shelves give this room greater aesthetic appeal.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Urban planners should consider both the practical function and aesthetic quality of public spaces.

words.definitionEn: Originating or living naturally in a place, rather than arriving later.
words.exampleDailyEn: These flowers are indigenous to the valley near our village.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Protecting indigenous languages helps preserve cultural knowledge that has been passed down through many generations.

words.definitionEn: The beginning of something, especially something unpleasant.
words.exampleDailyEn: The sudden onset of rain sent us running indoors.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular physical activity may delay the onset of certain chronic diseases and improve overall wellbeing.

words.definitionEn: a period of history marked by distinctive events or changes
words.exampleDailyEn: These old photographs capture an epoch of rapid change.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The development of agriculture marked a new epoch in human history, transforming settlement patterns and social organisation.

words.definitionEn: Having won a competition, battle, or struggle.
words.exampleDailyEn: The victorious team lifted the trophy above their heads.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Athletes who emerge victorious in international competitions often inspire younger generations to participate in sport.

words.definitionEn: care in speaking or acting to avoid embarrassment or harm
words.exampleDailyEn: Please use discretion when discussing her private life.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Teachers need some discretion to adapt classroom activities to the needs of individual learners.

words.definitionEn: an official responsible for a public service or commission
words.exampleDailyEn: The commissioner visited our neighbourhood to discuss road safety.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An independent commissioner should investigate public complaints and ensure that government agencies treat citizens fairly.

words.definitionEn: providing useful knowledge or helping someone understand something
words.exampleDailyEn: Watching my grandfather repair the clock was surprisingly instructive.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Comparing different countries' recycling systems can be instructive for policymakers seeking to reduce household waste.

words.definitionEn: To end something, or to come to an end.
words.exampleDailyEn: We decided to terminate our gym membership last month.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Employers should not terminate contracts without providing clear reasons and allowing workers sufficient time to respond.

words.definitionEn: to reach a conclusion using evidence rather than direct statements
words.exampleDailyEn: From her muddy shoes, I inferred she had been gardening.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers cannot infer that smaller classes improve learning without examining other factors affecting student performance.

words.definitionEn: A detailed description of how something must be designed or made.
words.exampleDailyEn: Check the specifications before buying a new laptop.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Clear building specifications help ensure that new housing meets safety standards and uses energy efficiently.

words.definitionEn: Stored under customs control until import duties are paid
words.exampleDailyEn: The imported coffee stays in a bonded warehouse nearby.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Bonded warehouses allow importers to delay paying duties until goods enter the domestic market.

words.definitionEn: Expressing ideas clearly, powerfully, and beautifully.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her eloquent speech moved everyone in the room.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The speaker offered an eloquent defence of public libraries as essential spaces for lifelong learning.

words.definitionEn: to stop something from having an effect
words.exampleDailyEn: This spray helps neutralize unpleasant smells in the kitchen.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Farmers sometimes add lime to acidic soil to neutralize excess acidity and improve conditions for crop growth.

words.definitionEn: The gradual removal of soil or rock by natural forces.
words.exampleDailyEn: Heavy rain caused erosion along the muddy river bank.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Planting trees can reduce soil erosion because their roots help hold the ground together during heavy rainfall.

words.definitionEn: Processed to remove unwanted substances.
words.exampleDailyEn: This recipe uses honey instead of refined white sugar.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public health campaigns often encourage people to reduce their consumption of foods containing large amounts of refined sugar.

words.definitionEn: A house, flat, or other place where someone lives
words.exampleDailyEn: Their small dwelling overlooks a quiet stretch of river.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Every new dwelling should meet energy efficiency standards to reduce household costs and environmental damage.

words.definitionEn: Worry intensely while trying to make a difficult decision
words.exampleDailyEn: I agonized over which course to choose all weekend.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many graduates agonize over whether to pursue further education or enter an increasingly competitive job market.

words.definitionEn: Carrying or holding a large amount of something.
words.exampleDailyEn: She arrived at the picnic laden with bags of food.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Trucks laden with construction materials contribute to congestion and increase road maintenance costs in rapidly expanding cities.

words.definitionEn: Relating to beauty or the appreciation of beautiful things.
words.exampleDailyEn: The curved wooden handle gives the kettle esthetic appeal.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Urban planners should balance the esthetic qualities of public spaces with accessibility and environmental sustainability.

words.definitionEn: an event in which a boat or sea animal becomes stuck
words.exampleDailyEn: Volunteers rushed to help after a whale stranding.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers investigate each mass stranding to understand why marine mammals sometimes become trapped in shallow coastal waters.

words.definitionEn: easily affected or harmed by something
words.exampleDailyEn: These young plants are particularly susceptible to frost damage.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Children may be more susceptible to online advertising because they lack experience in evaluating commercial claims.

words.definitionEn: to dig into ground and remove earth
words.exampleDailyEn: Workers excavated a deep hole for our new pool.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Archaeologists excavate ancient settlements to discover how earlier communities adapted to environmental changes and developed farming techniques.

words.definitionEn: a hit or kick before the ball touches the ground
words.exampleDailyEn: She won the tennis match with a sharp volley.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Learning to volley effectively helps young tennis players develop coordination and respond quickly under pressure.

words.definitionEn: the quality of being honest and following strong moral principles
words.exampleDailyEn: She showed integrity by returning the money she found.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Independent inspections help maintain the structural integrity of bridges and protect the public from preventable accidents.

words.definitionEn: Make sure that people obey a law or rule.
words.exampleDailyEn: The pool staff enforce strict rules about running indoors.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments must enforce environmental regulations consistently if they want industries to reduce pollution and protect public health.

words.definitionEn: the process of obtaining something or developing knowledge and skills
words.exampleDailyEn: Daily conversations helped with her acquisition of new vocabulary.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Early exposure to varied speech can support language acquisition and strengthen children's ability to communicate effectively.

words.definitionEn: To use something effectively for a particular purpose.
words.exampleDailyEn: We utilize the space under our stairs for storage.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools can utilize existing buildings more efficiently by sharing facilities with local communities after lessons.

words.definitionEn: A good reason explaining why something is acceptable or necessary.
words.exampleDailyEn: There is no justification for leaving this mess behind.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments must provide clear justification for policies that restrict individual freedom in the interests of public safety.

words.definitionEn: The process of passing something from one place to another.
words.exampleDailyEn: The mechanic checked the transmission before our long drive.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Improved ventilation in public buildings can reduce the transmission of certain infections and protect vulnerable people.

words.definitionEn: Someone who manages or provides large amounts of investment money
words.exampleDailyEn: A local financier helped fund the new theatre.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Financiers can accelerate the transition to clean energy by directing investment towards innovative renewable technologies.

words.definitionEn: To invent false information in order to deceive
words.exampleDailyEn: He fabricated an excuse for missing the family dinner.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers who fabricate evidence undermine public trust in science and may influence important policy decisions.

words.definitionEn: equally or in the same way throughout
words.exampleDailyEn: Spread the butter uniformly across the warm bread.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Environmental regulations must be applied uniformly to all companies to ensure fair competition.

words.definitionEn: Harmful or making success and progress more difficult.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our ferry was cancelled because of adverse weather conditions.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Prolonged exposure to traffic noise can have adverse effects on residents' sleep and mental health.

words.definitionEn: to happen at the same time
words.exampleDailyEn: My days off rarely coincide with my sister's.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Government investment should coincide with local priorities to ensure that public funds address genuine community needs.

words.definitionEn: a raised bank supporting transport routes or holding back water
words.exampleDailyEn: We walked along the embankment beside the swollen river.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Strengthening the river embankment could protect nearby homes from flooding as extreme rainfall becomes more frequent.

words.definitionEn: having conflicting feelings about someone or something
words.exampleDailyEn: I feel ambivalent about moving away from my family.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many consumers remain ambivalent about online shopping because convenience must be balanced against concerns about privacy.

words.definitionEn: To move around freely without a fixed route or destination.
words.exampleDailyEn: We roamed through the market until our feet hurt.

words.exampleIeltsEn: Treating minor ailments at local clinics can reduce pressure on hospitals and improve access to healthcare.

words.definitionEn: the deliberate murder of an important person, often for political reasons
words.exampleDailyEn: The museum guide explained how the assassination changed history.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The assassination of a political leader can trigger widespread instability and undermine public confidence in government.

words.definitionEn: To talk with someone and exchange thoughts.
words.exampleDailyEn: We conversed quietly while waiting for the train.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Language exchange programmes allow students to converse with native speakers and develop confidence in unfamiliar social situations.

words.definitionEn: Protection a country gives people escaping danger in another country.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her family sought asylum after fleeing their home country.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should assess asylum applications fairly while ensuring that vulnerable applicants have access to legal advice.

words.definitionEn: Likely or hoping to become something in the future.
words.exampleDailyEn: The agent showed three prospective buyers around our flat.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Universities should provide prospective students with clear information about tuition fees, course content, and career opportunities.

words.definitionEn: training or formal introduction when someone joins an organisation
words.exampleDailyEn: Our induction included a tour of the whole office.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A structured induction programme can help new employees understand workplace expectations and adapt to their roles.

words.definitionEn: to develop a plan, policy, or idea carefully
words.exampleDailyEn: We need to formulate a plan before moving house.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments should formulate transport policies that reduce congestion while ensuring affordable access for all residents.

words.definitionEn: to fix something firmly inside a surrounding material
words.exampleDailyEn: The artist embedded small shells in the wet clay.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools should embed environmental awareness in everyday lessons rather than discuss sustainability only on special occasions.

words.definitionEn: The usual or expected standard of quality or performance.
words.exampleDailyEn: I'm feeling below par, so I'll stay home tonight.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Investment in teacher training could bring educational outcomes in disadvantaged areas up to par with wealthier districts.

words.definitionEn: Describe someone or something in a false or misleading way
words.exampleDailyEn: That photograph misrepresents the size of our tiny kitchen.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Advertisements can misrepresent the environmental benefits of products, making it harder for consumers to make informed decisions.

words.definitionEn: happening repeatedly, often at regular intervals
words.exampleDailyEn: The old boiler needs periodic checks to keep working safely.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Periodic assessments allow teachers to identify learning difficulties before students fall significantly behind their classmates.

words.definitionEn: The state of being easily harmed, affected, or attacked.
words.exampleDailyEn: The storm exposed the vulnerability of our old roof.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Investing in flood defences can reduce the vulnerability of coastal communities to increasingly severe storms.

words.definitionEn: having no clear purpose, plan, or direction
words.exampleDailyEn: We spent the afternoon on an aimless walk.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Without clear learning goals, students may engage in aimless online browsing rather than developing useful research skills.

words.definitionEn: A change in the route or use of something.
words.exampleDailyEn: The road diversion took us past a beautiful lake.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The diversion of public funds away from education could limit opportunities for children in disadvantaged communities.

words.definitionEn: comfort received when you feel sad or disappointed
words.exampleDailyEn: After losing the match, she found consolation in music.
words.exampleIeltsEn: For workers facing unemployment, emotional support offers some consolation, but practical assistance remains essential for long-term recovery.

words.definitionEn: an office representing a country and helping its citizens abroad
words.exampleDailyEn: She contacted the consulate after losing her passport abroad.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A consulate can provide essential assistance to citizens who encounter legal or administrative difficulties while travelling abroad.

words.definitionEn: Too brightly coloured or heavily decorated to look attractive.
words.exampleDailyEn: He wore a gaudy jacket covered in shiny sequins.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Some residents argue that gaudy decorations in historic districts undermine the visual character of traditional buildings.

words.definitionEn: temporarily inactive but able to become active again
words.exampleDailyEn: These plants stay dormant until the weather becomes warmer.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Although the volcano has remained dormant for centuries, scientists continue to monitor it for signs of renewed activity.

words.definitionEn: to make pain, suffering, or a problem less severe
words.exampleDailyEn: A warm bath helped alleviate the ache in my shoulders.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Expanding affordable housing could alleviate pressure on low-income families and reduce the risk of homelessness.

words.definitionEn: Forced absence from one's own country, often for political reasons
words.exampleDailyEn: After years in exile, she finally returned home.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many writers living in exile use literature to preserve cultural traditions and describe their experiences of displacement.

words.definitionEn: To free people or places from control or imprisonment.
words.exampleDailyEn: The rescued prisoners cheered when soldiers liberated the camp.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Accessible public transport can liberate older people from dependence on relatives and enable greater participation in community life.

words.definitionEn: To give official permission for someone to do something.
words.exampleDailyEn: Only the manager can authorize a refund this large.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Local authorities may authorize new housing developments only after assessing their likely effects on traffic and public services.

words.definitionEn: The process of making something stronger or more effective.
words.exampleDailyEn: The old garden wall needs reinforcement before winter arrives.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Positive reinforcement can encourage children to develop healthy habits without relying on punishment.

words.definitionEn: the act of keeping something or preventing someone from leaving
words.exampleDailyEn: Our manager improved staff retention by offering flexible hours.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular revision and adequate sleep can improve the retention of information among students preparing for examinations.

words.definitionEn: Suggested or understood without being directly stated.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her welcoming smile was an implicit invitation to join.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many workplaces have implicit expectations about overtime, which can make employees reluctant to leave on time.

words.definitionEn: to cause someone or something to enter a particular state
words.exampleDailyEn: A cracked screen rendered my old phone unusable.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Rising sea levels could render some coastal settlements uninhabitable unless governments invest in effective flood protection.

words.definitionEn: Able to pay all the money that is owed.
words.exampleDailyEn: Careful budgeting kept our small shop solvent this year.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Businesses must remain solvent during economic downturns while continuing to meet their obligations to employees and suppliers.

words.definitionEn: To make something widely known, liked, or used.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her cooking videos helped popularize this simple bean soup.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public broadcasters can popularize scientific knowledge by explaining complex discoveries through accessible documentaries and practical demonstrations.

words.definitionEn: changing in a constant ratio to another quantity
words.exampleDailyEn: The delivery fee is proportional to the parcel's weight.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Environmental taxes should be proportional to the damage caused, encouraging businesses to adopt cleaner production methods.

words.definitionEn: Unable to support much plant growth.
words.exampleDailyEn: Only a few bushes grew on the barren hillside.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Unsustainable farming can turn productive fields into barren land, threatening food security and forcing rural communities to relocate.

words.definitionEn: Burning or shining brightly.
words.exampleDailyEn: The candles were still alight when we arrived.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Passengers should wait until the bus has stopped completely before they alight from the vehicle.

words.definitionEn: To make something seem small by comparison.
words.exampleDailyEn: The new tower dwarfs every house on our street.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The long-term costs of environmental damage may dwarf the immediate profits generated by industrial expansion.

words.definitionEn: To comfort someone who feels sad or disappointed.
words.exampleDailyEn: Lena tried to console her brother after his team lost.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Teachers should console disappointed students while helping them develop practical strategies for improving their academic performance.

words.definitionEn: A powered leisure boat with space for sleeping.
words.exampleDailyEn: We spent the weekend aboard a small cabin cruiser.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The growing popularity of holidays aboard a cruiser has increased demand for moorings along inland waterways.

words.definitionEn: write or carve words on an object, often permanently
words.exampleDailyEn: The jeweller inscribed our initials inside the silver ring.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Communities often inscribe memorial stones with personal stories to preserve local history for future generations.

words.definitionEn: To make someone or something completely wet
words.exampleDailyEn: A sudden downpour drenched us on the way home.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Intense storms can drench farmland within minutes, increasing surface runoff and carrying valuable topsoil into nearby rivers.

words.definitionEn: A short period of illness or intense activity
words.exampleDailyEn: A bout of flu kept me home all week.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular exercise may help reduce bouts of anxiety and improve overall mental health among university students.

words.definitionEn: Acts intended to destroy a national, ethnic, racial, or religious group.
words.exampleDailyEn: We visited a memorial to the victims of genocide.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Education about past acts of genocide can help societies recognise prejudice and strengthen their commitment to human rights.

words.definitionEn: The state of being most numerous, powerful, or influential.
words.exampleDailyEn: The predominance of blue gives this room a cool feel.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The predominance of private cars in urban transport creates challenges for efforts to reduce air pollution.

words.definitionEn: the act of following a rule, law, or request
words.exampleDailyEn: The inspector checked our kitchen for compliance with hygiene rules.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular inspections can improve compliance with environmental regulations and reduce pollution from industrial facilities.

words.definitionEn: relating to written words or the wording of a document
words.exampleDailyEn: The editor made several textual changes to my story.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Students should support their interpretations with textual evidence rather than rely solely on personal reactions to a novel.

words.definitionEn: relating to plans for achieving important long-term goals
words.exampleDailyEn: We made a strategic decision to save before moving.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Strategic investment in public transport can reduce congestion and support economic growth over the long term.

words.definitionEn: Likely or willing to think or act a certain way.
words.exampleDailyEn: I'm inclined to stay home and cook tonight.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Consumers may be more inclined to repair appliances when affordable local repair services are readily available.

words.definitionEn: a device controlling the flow of liquid or gas
words.exampleDailyEn: Turn this valve to stop water entering the tank.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Replacing damaged heart valves can improve patients' quality of life and reduce the risk of serious complications.
